gaps.question: Rally X with no site of type X in a country: what happens to that country's pool?
gaps.engine: The pool is emptied first, then nothing lands: its agents never leave the adversary's supply. In effect the pool goes back to the supply and that round's agents are lost to that country. (A cordoned country is the exception: its pool is not touched and waits for the next Rally.)
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/adversary.rs:1063-1076 (pool set to 0 at 1067, then rally_plan returns None, tallied adversary.rally_nowhere, continue); plan.rs:277-280 (rally_plan returns None when the country has no site of the type); cordon skip adversary.rs:1059-1062
gaps.book_answers: no. §6 step 3 says only "The pool is now empty." and does not cover the case with no site.

gaps.question: Buy energy, 'each city once a round': per player or once for all players?
gaps.engine: Once for all players. The mark is kept per city, not per player: once anyone buys a neutral city's energy, no one else can buy it that round. The mark clears at the end of the round.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/standard.rs:188-207 (bought_key(h) is keyed on the hex only; energy_for_sale checks it), :534-540 (sets it); board/mod.rs:135 (BOUGHT is a round mark, cleared each round)
gaps.book_answers: no. §8 table, Buy energy: "each city once a round" does not say whether that is per player.

gaps.question: Does a completed megaproject pay once or every round? Where do station cubes go after completion, and does anything pay per cube later?
gaps.engine: It pays once, at the end of the income step in which it reaches 8 or more cubes. Every cube on it pays its owner once, overflow included, then all of its cubes are cleared and it is marked complete for good. After that, a player's station puts its 2 cubes a round straight onto its owner's board as research cubes, and a neutral station's cube is lost. Nothing pays per cube again: research cubes are just a resource you spend (converters, insight, Peer Review, threats).
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/production.rs:384-427 (complete_projects: skips a project already done, zeroes every cube key at 398-403, sets project_done, runs the payout once per cube at 414-421); :363-374 (station_cubes: before completion onto the project, after it onto the owner as ResearchCubes, neutral lost)
gaps.book_answers: partly. §9 step 3: "Once it is complete, a player's cubes go onto their board as research cubes, and a neutral station's are lost." and step 4: "A megaproject holding 8 cubes or more completes: every cube on it pays, overflow included". Neither sentence says the payout happens only once or that the cubes leave the card.

gaps.question: If the leftover after a tip still fills the track (1-2 players), does it tip again at once?
gaps.engine: Yes. After each tip the engine checks both tracks again, Discord first, and tips again while a track still holds a full tip's worth. It repeats up to 64 times in one check. A tip removes exactly one tip's worth and the rest carries over (carry 2).
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/alignment.rs:554-586 ('tips loop: a track at capacity tips, then continue 'tips rechecks); :389-401 (tip removes capacity.min(held)); configs/baseline.json alignment.carry 2
gaps.book_answers: partly. §12 Tipping: "The rest stays on the track toward its next tip" and "A card that fills a track again tips it again." The book covers a card refilling the track but not a leftover that is already full.

gaps.question: A hardening token on a hex with both a player's facility and a node: is it usable for either? Does saving one save the other?
gaps.engine: Either. A hardening token on the hex is offered against the destruction of any piece there: the node or the facility, whoever owns each. In war, the node is attacked only if its factory is actually destroyed. So saving the factory (with the token, an ambassador, Aegis or Shelter) also saves the node. If the factory goes, the token stays on the hex as the node's shield (it is removed only if no node remains) and can then be spent for the node. A troop never strikes the node, because nodes are troop targets only at stage 4+, which never comes. A Corrupt line attacks only the node, and the token can save it.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/destroy.rs:48-66 (guards: Harden whenever HARDEN>0 on the hex, any kind), :130-139 (the token is removed with a facility only when no node is on the hex); troops.rs:65-73 (war: the node is attacked only `if destroy_piece(...FACTORY...)` returned true); troops.rs:247 with baseline troop_node 4 (nodes are troop targets only from stage 4)
gaps.book_answers: mostly. §13 protection order: "a hardening token on the hex (on a hex with your node it is called a shield)". §11 War 3: "If it is destroyed, it adds 1 Discord, and any node on its hex would be destroyed too". That implies saving the factory saves the node, but the book never says outright that one token serves either piece.

gaps.question: Can an agent and a player's ambassador ever share a hex (so Claim/Liberate's '+1 per agent' applies where my ambassador stands)?
gaps.engine: No. Every arrival cancels one for one: an agent landing, converging or being moved onto ambassadors removes one of them; an ambassador arriving (Dispatch, a card move, Gather/Push, Convert) on agents removes one agent and is itself removed. No code path adds either piece without that check. So a site never holds both, and '+1 per agent' applies only on a site where none of your ambassadors stand. (Several ambassadors gathered onto 1 agent: the first cancels it and the rest stand on an agent-free hex.)
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/adversary.rs:1207-1215 (arrive), :1423-1434 (converge_one); board/ambassadors.rs:23-30 (place_ambassador), :35-50 (agent_cancels); effects/moves.rs:86-101 (arrive for moved pieces); effects/endgame.rs:52-54 (Convert places through place_ambassador); a grep of add_tokens finds no other place where ADV_AMBASSADOR or ambassador(s) is added
gaps.book_answers: partly, by implication. §8: "Every contact is one for one. When an agent lands on a hex where players' ambassadors stand, it and one of them are removed ... When your ambassador arrives on a hex with agents, it removes one of them and is removed itself." The book never says that the two can never share a hex.

gaps.question: Take down a botnet: must the hex be in reach, or only have the player's ambassador on it?
gaps.engine: Only your ambassador on it. Reach is not checked. The ambassador got there by a move that was in reach, but it may stay there after your nodes are gone.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/standard.rs:209-213 (botnet_targets: BOTNET>0 && your ambassador on the hex; no in_reach), :464
gaps.book_answers: partly, and in conflict. §8 table: "remove a botnet from a hex where your ambassador stands (the ambassador stays)". But §2 Reach says "everything you target on the map must be in your reach", which suggests reach is needed.

gaps.question: Difficulty 'Unpaid threats: +4 compute each' (level 2+): what happens and when does the compute reach projects?
gaps.engine: From level 2 (adversary.board_difficulty_at 2), each threat that takes effect unpaid in step F gives the adversary 4 compute, right after its harm resolves. A threat that only waits does not. The compute sits beside the projects and goes onto them in the next adversary turn's compute step (step 12), with the rest of the round's compute. No project resolves earlier.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/threats/mod.rs:421-450 (skips waiting threats; after effects::run adds adversary::threat_compute); adversary.rs:329-335 (threat_compute = board rules plus the difficulty line from board_difficulty_at); :809-819 (gain_compute only banks WAITING), :825-875 (compute_step pours it); content/adversary.json:47-58 (difficulty threat_compute 4); configs/baseline.json:113
gaps.book_answers: partly. §21 table: "+4 compute each". §6 step 12 and §17: "every compute made since the last compute step (threats taking effect, ...) ... waits beside the projects until then." The book never says that 'Unpaid threats' means threats taking effect in step F, or that a waiting threat doesn't pay.

gaps.question: Does every city build a factory every round in growth? Does a blocked city build? Does a destroyed factory free its zone?
gaps.engine: Yes. In growth every city, of any owner and blocked or not, builds one factory if an industrial zone next to it is free (no factory, no station, no land corruption). A node, an agent or a marker on the zone does not stop it. A destroyed factory's piece leaves the map (its token and its owner's cube come off), so the zone is free and a city next to it rebuilds there in the next growth.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/production.rs:218-259 (grow_factories: every city, no blocked check); common.rs:158-162 (free_zones: industrial, !has_building, no LAND_CORRUPTION); destroy.rs:126-133 (destroyed: the FACTORY token and its cube removed)
gaps.book_answers: partly. §9 step 7: "Every city, blocked or not, builds one factory on a free industrial zone (one with no factory, station or land corruption) next to it". §13 says only "A destroyed facility takes its owner's cube with it". That the factory piece leaves and frees the zone is not stated.

gaps.question: Corrupt X: do agents on an adversary-owned site next to a target move onto it? Do agents already on one target move to another?
gaps.engine: An adversary-owned site is not a target, so its agents move onto a target next to it like any others. Agents on a target, including one a prohibition holds, stay where they are. An agent next to several targets goes where the players choose.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/plan.rs:102-113 (corrupt_target excludes corrupted), :157-168 (converge: a hex that is itself a target is skipped; every other hex with agents is a source), adversary.rs:1385-1395 (players choose)
gaps.book_answers: yes. §15: "A target is a place of that type the adversary doesn't own" and step 1: "Every agent next to a target moves onto it ... agents already on a target stay."

gaps.question: Round 1: do Round start (setting insight) and Sway run before the first adversary turn?
gaps.engine: Yes. The game starts at the end of round 0, so round 1 runs every module's round_start (insight is set) and then the phases in order: alignment.sway, then the adversary's event. At setup Sway adds nothing, since there is no land corruption and the Militarist's discord_drip is 0.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/rules.rs:343-344 (new game: round 0, phase = len), :721-737 (round += 1, round_start for every module); configs/baseline.json:366-367 (round starts "alignment.sway", then "adversary.event"); economy.rs:189-200 (insight set at round start); alignment.rs:520-527 (Sway: drip + land corruption)
gaps.book_answers: partly. §4's table lists Round start, then A Sway, then B the adversary's turn. §3 ends "The game starts with the adversary's turn, before anyone acts.", which reads as if the adversary's turn comes first.

gaps.question: Vigil: which marches exist besides step 10? Does a troop that couldn't move, or that removed an ambassador on its last step, end its march and pay?
gaps.engine: There are two marches: the adversary turn's march (step 10) and an immediate march that a threat prints (the march_now op, used by Total War). Vigil pays in both. Any troop that is not used up ends its march where it stands and pays if that hex is next to a Vigil player's node. That includes a troop with no path (it stops), a troop that spent its steps removing ambassadors, and a troop with no target at all. Only a troop used up by striking, or a standing troop that doesn't march, does not pay.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/troops.rs:115-130 (march), :134-143 (march_now), :147-228 (alive stays true unless a strike spends the troop at 193-196; no path breaks at 198-200; ambassador removal continues at 168-187; the Vigil check at 215-224); effects/new_ops.rs:131 (march_now); content/threats.json:1027 (Total War)
gaps.book_answers: partly. §5 Vigil: "It pays once per troop per march, in any march; a troop used up striking has no end to its march." It doesn't name the marches or say that a stuck troop or one that removed an ambassador still pays.

gaps.question: Solo: are the 4 cards taken in the draft kept free or paid like any keep?
gaps.engine: Paid like any keep: 1 insight per tier-1 card, 2 per tier-2 card (1 with the keep upgrade, less with Science discounts), with any insight short paid at 5 credits each. The keep price has no solo case. Solo only means nothing is passed, so all 4 cards reach the keep step.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/cards/price.rs:13-32 (keep_need: no seat-count case); cards/play.rs:10-17 (keep_price, shortfall in credits)
gaps.book_answers: no, and misleading. §7: "Solo, you keep all 4." and §22: "You keep all 4 cards you take in the draft." Both read as free keeps.

gaps.question: Does a troop mustered onto a player's factory hex strike it in the very next march? Does a troop landing on an ambassador's hex do anything on landing?
gaps.engine: Yes. Muster (step 4) comes before the march (step 10) in the same turn. On its first step the troop finds the target on its own hex and strikes it (protections apply), unless an ambassador is there. Landing does nothing. But at its first step a troop standing with an ambassador removes one (the players choose whose) instead of striking, and strikes with its second step. So your ambassador on your factory is removed rather than spent as the factory's protection.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/adversary.rs:1259-1262 (place_troop just adds the token), :1470-1531 (land_troops: lowest factory of any owner); troops.rs:166-196 (step: remove an ambassador on the hex first, else strike a target on or next to it); configs/baseline.json round order (adversary.build before board.march)
gaps.book_answers: partly. §6: "if an ambassador (any player's) stands on the troop's hex, the troop removes one ... else, if a target is on or next to the troop's hex, the troop strikes it". The book does not say that a troop mustered onto your factory strikes it in the same turn.

gaps.question: Discord tip: one ambassador on a neutral factory with 2 bases needing drones, which drone is stopped and who decides? What happens with several players' ambassadors on a base that is not full?
gaps.engine: Factory: only bases with room count (a full base takes nothing). While an ambassador stands on the factory and an open base remains, one ambassador is spent per base. If there are more open bases than ambassadors, the players choose which base's drone each one stops; otherwise it is the first base. The ambassador spent is always the earliest in player order's (no choice). Base: each drone that comes to a base that is not full is stopped by one ambassador there, the earliest in player order (no choice). One ambassador is spent per drone, so 2 factories sending drones spend 2. A full base takes no drone and spends no ambassador.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/production.rs:50-86 (tip_corp_troops: open = bases below cap; choose when open.len() > standing, else index 0; player_ambassador picks the seat), :14-31 (corp_troops_at: break at cap before any ambassador; else player_ambassador spent per drone); common.rs:123-125 (player_ambassador = lowest seat)
gaps.book_answers: partly, and misplaced. §19: "if it can't stop them all, the players choose which base goes without" covers the factory. The parenthesis "(with several players' ambassadors there, the earliest in player order is spent)" is attached to the full-base sentence, where nothing is spent. It belongs to a base that is not full.

gaps.question: Wall: does an adversary factory on the Protector's node hex make its troop there? Can a corrupted city build an adversary factory onto a hex with the Protector's node?
gaps.engine: Yes to both. Factory output places the troop on the factory's own hex with no Wall check. That troop can't strike there, so it walks off. Growth's free-zone test ignores nodes, so a corrupted city can build an adversary factory on an industrial zone that holds the Protector's node.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/production.rs:200-209 (factory_output: place_troop, no walled check); troops.rs:233-238 (walled hex has no targets), :342-344 (a troop on a walled hex walks off); common.rs:158-162 (free_zones has no node test); production.rs:224-242
gaps.book_answers: partly. §5 Wall: "An adversary factory on that hex still makes its troop there; it can't strike that hex, and marches off as usual." That a factory can be built there is implied only by §9's definition of a free zone.

gaps.question: A corruption marker on a city 'counts as an agent there': only for corruption, or also for Claim/Liberate prices and blocking?
gaps.engine: Only for corruption: natural corruption and a Corrupt X line's count against a city (not a node target, and the marker never moves). Claim and Liberate prices count agents only, and so does blocking (a city is dark only with an agent on it or a blackout).
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/plan.rs:115-118 (held adds MARKER for non-node city), adversary.rs:1397; board/ambassadors.rs:100-116 (claim_cost/liberate_cost: ADV_AMBASSADOR only); production.rs:285-287 (city_dark: agents or blackout); standard.rs:199-207
gaps.book_answers: no. §6 and §15 say "A corruption marker on a city counts as an agent there" with no limit stated.

gaps.question: What 'income track' do cards move (op names), and what does an arrow-down do?
gaps.engine: Each player has a per-resource production counter (economy.production.<seat>.<resource>) that pays every round in upkeep (insight at round start). Card ops that raise it: production {resource, amount} (37 uses: credits, energy, chips, insight, research_cubes), production_per_tag (10 uses, counted once when played) and copy_income. An arrow down would lower it permanently: a negative production or a card's lowers cost. No card in content/cards.json prints one at revision 77.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/op.rs:705-716 (Production, ProductionPerTag), :813-816 (CopyIncome); effects/mod.rs:199-201; economy.rs:40-50 (production_key, raise_production); face.rs:111-119 (track_move: raise/lower), :517-522, :1131-1133 (lowers); content.rs:363-367; content/cards.json (no negative amount, no lowers)
gaps.book_answers: no. §23 Marks: "Brown box with a track arrow | move your income track once: arrow up, raise it; arrow down, lower it". The income track itself is never defined.

gaps.question: A city with a player's node and 2 agents: does the node go while the city stays? Order in natural corruption?
gaps.engine: Yes. Natural corruption runs cities, then stations, then factories, then node hexes. A city with 2 agents is short of its number (4, or 3 from level 1), so it doesn't corrupt. Then the node check finds 2 agents and the node is destroyed (protections apply). The 2 agents go to the supply and the city is untouched. Had the city reached its number, it would have corrupted first and taken the node with it (that leaves no marker).
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/adversary.rs:1440-1463 (order City, Station, Factory, Node), :1330-1343 (corrupt_node: agents off, node destroyed, nothing else), :1292-1308
gaps.book_answers: yes. §15: "Then each hex with a player's node and 2 agents loses that node (§13 still applies); the agents go back to the supply and the site there, if any, is untouched."

gaps.question: Effects 'fire every time, with no limit': is there any per-round cap?
gaps.engine: No per-round cap. Each trigger fires once per action that sets it off (a per-tag play trigger pays per tag), every time, for as long as the building is uncovered.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/cards/triggers.rs:1-4 ("fire each time their event happens, with no per-round limit"), :37-56 (fire), :212 and :225 (once per action)
gaps.book_answers: yes. §7: "An Effect ... fires every time, with no limit: once for each action that sets it off". §23: "Every Effect fires once per action".

gaps.question: Lines that corrupt a named site (Station Seizure, Overrun): does a player's station need 2 agents and no ambassador, does it flip outright, or does an agent land?
gaps.engine: It depends on the op. Station Seizure (threat, flip_station force:true) corrupts the token's station outright, a player's too, with no agent condition. Overrun (corrupt_city) corrupts the token's city outright if it isn't the adversary's yet. Factory Occupation (seize_factory) takes the factory outright. Only the unforced flip_station (the Station Coup project) defends a player's station. The engine condition is `if g.tokens(h, ADV_AMBASSADOR) < need || player_ambassador(g, h).is_some()` with need = adversary.station_flip_at = 2. Short of that, 1 agent lands on it instead (cancelled by an ambassador there). Otherwise the 2 agents are removed and it flips. A neutral station flips outright. None of these checks a firewall.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/effects/new_ops.rs:20-21 (force true -> force_flip), :312-330 (force_flip: corrupt_hex directly), :335-341 (corrupt_city), :156-162 (SeizeFactory); adversary.rs:1539-1569 (corrupt_station condition at 1541-1543); team.rs:39-68; content/threats.json Station Seizure (flip_station force:true), Overrun (corrupt_city); content/projects.json:260-268 (Station Coup); configs/baseline.json:111
gaps.book_answers: no. §6 says only "some threats and projects corrupt the site they name".

gaps.question: Location tokens with two types: printed order? A fewer-sites-first rule so both fit?
gaps.engine: Printed order first. Each token goes on the most-pressured site of its type that is not the adversary's and not already taken (tie: lower hex). If that leaves a token unplaced, the engine retries with the type that has fewer candidate sites first and keeps whichever try placed more tokens. A type that still has no free site gets no token.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/threats/near.rs:68-102 (assign in printed order; retry sorted by sites().len() at 88-98), :44-53 (sites: not corrupted)
gaps.book_answers: partly. §18: "For each printed type, the token goes on the place of that type that isn't the adversary's with the most adversary pieces ... A threat's two tokens never share a hex." Neither the printed order nor the fewer-sites-first retry is stated.

gaps.question: Is the project deck shuffled at setup? Are military bases printed on tiles or placed by the layout?
gaps.engine: Shuffled: setup shuffles every project into one deck, then deals into the slots. Bases are not tile data. The engine places them from the player-count layout's printed fronts: for each front, on an open hex of that country touching land of the other country, holding no setup piece, station site, industrial zone or starting hex. It takes the lowest-numbered free candidate, and fronts with the fewest candidates choose first. So a tile's base hexes depend on which countries it borders in that layout.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/adversary.rs:385-389 (shuffle the project deck, deal_projects); crates/aic-core/src/map.rs:157-230 (place_bases); content/map.json layouts[].fronts (no base field on countries)
gaps.book_answers: no for the shuffle: §3 step 3 says "Deal projects into the adversary board's slots", and step 4's shuffle list leaves out the project deck. Bases: §2 says "printed on an open hex by the border", which doesn't match a layout-dependent placement.

gaps.question: Does any 'embargo' state forbid claiming a site in the engine? Which threat, what op, is it printed?
gaps.engine: The engine has the state: RoundFlag::Embargo, on a hex or a country, refuses Claim there (and card claims of stations). But no content at revision 77 sets it: no flag op names embargo. The threat named Embargo only creates 2 agents on its factory token and makes the nearest player pay 2 energy or discard 2 cards. So in play nothing forbids a claim.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/ambassadors.rs:10-12 (can_claim checks hex_flagged Embargo); op.rs:514, :521; board/mod.rs:99-100, :116-118; board/view.rs:10; content: the only flag ops are blackout (content/adversary.json:695, content/projects.json:350); content/threats.json:702 (Embargo: create 2 at location + requisition)
gaps.book_answers: no (and nothing printed needs it).

gaps.question: Shelter: exactly what does it stop, and from when to when?
gaps.engine: It is a country flag set to 1 when the power or card resolves in the action phase and cleared in cleanup (step H). While it is up, every destruction that goes through the protection order in that country is stopped with nothing spent: nodes and facilities hit by a troop strike, war (so no war Discord either), a threat's or card's destroy, and the node a corruption would destroy. Not stopped: a cube changing owner (corruption, seizure, flips), ambassadors removed by a troop or by corruption, agents, and nodes removed directly rather than destroyed. Those direct removals are a threat's pay-or-lose-a-node choice, a node given up as a threat payment, and Regime Change's nodes on and next to its city. A second Shelter in the same country does nothing.
gaps.evidence: crates/aic-core/src/modules/board/mod.rs:228-231 (shelter sets the flag to 1), :517-529 (cleanup counts it down); destroy.rs:74-79 (destroy_piece returns early under Shelter); adversary.rs:1300-1313 (corruption's cube flip and ambassador removal outside destroy_piece); direct lose_node calls bypassing it: effects/new_ops.rs:344, :504, :512; threats/ops.rs:133; threats/counter.rs:408; effects/targets.rs:119-124
gaps.book_answers: partly. §13: "Shelter on that country this round ... stops it, automatically, spending nothing. It lasts from the action phase to cleanup, so it covers production, threats and war, never the adversary's turn." §20: "in any one country, nothing can be destroyed this round". This overstates it: cube flips, ambassador removal and node losses chosen or paid are not stopped.
